text:
Michael: Heads-up — Q3 perf planning thread. Need to prioritize between smart routing, adaptive batching, and KV prefetch for a couple SLA-driven pilots. Also need clear launch criteria.
Raja: Quick context? which pilots + what SLAs?
Michael: Two enterprise pilots (fintech + search infra). Both saw tail latency spikes during bursts. Customer ask: 99.9% < 300ms for embeddings endpoints and < 150ms for short-chat flows.
Sophia: Noted. High-level tradeoffs: batching => better throughput/cost but increases median and can worsen p99; prefetch/KV helps tails but ups memory/GPU footprint; routing to smaller quantized variants helps tail and cost but risks quality regressions.
Alice: Agree. Proposal for prioritization: 1) Short experiment to quantify p50/p95/p99 cost delta for adaptive batching knobs. 2) Lightweight KV prefetch canary with conservative memory cap. 3) Routing policy prototype that falls back to a quantized model only on overloaded hosts.
Ben: For experiments we need metrics and gating rules. Suggest: p99 improvement >= 20% OR cost increase <= 10% with no quality regressions on eval prompts. Canary window = 48h, traffic slice = 5%.
Michael: Good. Also include rollout gate for regressions: automated eval suite must pass and synthetic latency injection shouldn’t cause >5% request failures.
Sophia: Can we sketch config we want to test? e.g.:
```json
{
  "adaptive_batching": {"max_batch_ms": 8, "min_batch_size": 1, "threshold_qps": 150},
  "kv_prefetch": {"enabled": true, "max_memory_mb": 1200, "ttl_seconds": 30},
  "routing": {"fallback_quantized": "llama-2-q4", "cpu_fallback": false}
}
```
Raja: That helps. Who owns the KV canary and telemetry dashboard? Need dashboards for p50/p95/p99, token cost, GPU mem, and quality (eval set IR).
Alice: I'll own KV canary + dashboard. Ben can own adaptive batching experiment. Michael will own routing prototype + rollout plan.
Ben: For adaptive batching, we should test static vs adaptive thresholds and measure added latency percentiles and token-efficiency. I’ll add a short A/B plan.
Michael: Timeline: spike work this week, canaries next week, decision meeting on Mon 2255001340 (schedule invite incoming).
deploy-bot: canary created: canary-id=canary-2255a, traffic=5%, start=2255001300
Sophia: FYI for cost modeling: run a synthetic workload that mirrors pilot qps bursts (use bursty poisson with peak 4x baseline).
Raja: Also capture warm vs cold KV hit rates; include KV hit ratio and tail latency correlation.
Alice: noted. I’ll add those panels.
Ben: One more: fallback routing should be pluggable per-customer via policy so we can respect pilot constraints.
Michael: Yes — policy-driven routing + per-customer rollout. Final ask: draft launch criteria before canary: 1) p99 target met on pilot traffic; 2) cost delta within threshold; 3) no eval regressions; 4) runbook updated.
Sophia: + add SLA docs and rollback steps in runbook.
Michael: Great — thanks all. Will post PR with experiment configs and invite to Monday sync.
Raja: thanks :thumbsup:
Alice: thanks — starting dashboard prep.
Ben: adding A/B plan to docs.
deploy-bot: canary health: running (0 errors)
Michael: closing loop — see you at the sync.
